title: Crush It!
author: Gary Vaynerchuk
blurb: Gary Vaynerchuk argues that the internet has made it possible for almost anyone to earn a living from their passion. He draws on his own story of using online video, through his show Wine Library TV, to grow his family's wine business and build a personal brand. His formula is simple to say and hard to do. Love your family, work extremely hard, and live your passion. He urges readers to find the subject they could talk about endlessly, build a brand around it, and create content on blogs, video, podcasts and social platforms. Authenticity matters more than polish. Caring for your community, by answering comments and joining conversations, is what builds trust. Most people should start on nights and weekends, stay patient, and monetize later. Above all, he values legacy over quick money.

lessons.t: Your Passion Can Pay the Bills
lessons.b: The internet lets ordinary people build real careers around what they love, as Gary did with Wine Library TV.
Gary's core formula is to love your family, work superhard, and live your passion, in that order.
Everyone now needs a personal brand, because people connect with and buy from individuals they trust.
Being genuinely yourself on camera or in writing beats a slick, imitated persona, because authenticity is what makes people stay.

lessons.t: Pick Your Platform and Create Content
lessons.b: Choose the medium that fits your strengths, whether writing, video or audio, and produce valuable content consistently.
Answering every comment and joining conversations elsewhere online is how you turn viewers into a loyal community.
issues: scene 8: The closing challenge scene is almost entirely text. The only picture is a small two-bubble icon in the top-right corner, so the challenge itself (reply to every comment, join a conversation beyond your page) is not shown. (fix: Add a real illustration on the right half. For example, a comment list with every reply icon checked, plus an arrow leading out to an external forum card. Alternatively, enlarge the chat icon to about 300px and pair it with a small 'your page → elsewhere' graphic.)

scene 2: The clock reads 6:00, which does not suggest 'late into the night'. The time conflicts with the moon and the narration. (fix: Set the hands to a late hour, such as 11:50 or around 2:00 a.m., so the clock matches the late-night message.)

lessons.b: Start on nights and weekends, be patient before monetizing, and value legacy over quick money to make your passion last.
